raw: • State Larmor's formula for the power radiated by a charge q undergoing acceleration a.
(빈 슬라이드)

Dipole Approximation
• When there are many particles with different positions r_i, velocities v_i, and charges q_i, we can find the radiation field at large distances by simply adding together the E_rad from each particle.
  – However, the differences in retarded time make it difficult to obtain E_rad.
• When many charged particles are in a small volume with size (r′ ≪ λ), the differences in retarded time across the source are negligible ➔ dipole approximation.
• Then, E_rad(x,t) = Σ_i (q_i/c)[n̂×{n̂×β̇_i}/R_i]_ret = [n̂×{n̂×p̈}/(c²R₀)]_ret
  where the dipole moment is p ≡ Σ_i q_i x_i = ∫_{V₀} ρ(x′,t) x′ d³x′
  ➡ dP/dΩ = p̈² sin²Θ/(4πc³),  P = 2p̈²/(3c³)
[그림: 회색 원(소스 부피 V₀) 안에 원점 O와 위치 x′, ρ(x′,t′), j(x′,t′); 멀리 관측점 P(φ(x,t), A(x,t))까지 벡터 x와 x−x′]

For a Free Electron
• We apply the dipole formula to the radiation from a free charge in response to an incident electromagnetic wave.
• Consider a free electron exposed to EM radiation.
[그림: 왼쪽에서 k̂ 방향으로 들어오는 파동 E = x̂E₀cos ω₀t (for polarized E field), 전하 q가 위아래(x̂)로 진동, 진동축과 각 Θ를 이루는 n̂ 방향으로 나가는 scattered E field (polarized)]
• EOM under the Lorenz force (non-relativistic case)
  F = m_e ẍ = e(E + (v/c)×B) ≈ eE = eE₀cos(ω₀t)  ➡ ẍ = (eE₀/m_e) cos(ω₀t)
• Angular distribution of the radiated power is dP/dΩ = e²|ẍ|² sin²Θ/(4πc³)

Thomson Scattering Cross Section
• Time-averaged angular distribution of power ⟨dP/dΩ⟩ = (e²/4πc³) sin²Θ · (e²E₀²/m_e²)⟨cos²(ω₀t)⟩ = e⁴E₀² sin²Θ/(8πm_e²c³)
• Total radiated power is ⟨P⟩ = e⁴E₀²/(3m_e²c³)
• The incident flux is ⟨S⟩ = (c/4π)⟨E²⟩ = (cE₀²/4π)⟨cos²(ω₀t)⟩ = cE₀²/8π
• The differential scattering cross section is given by dσ_sca/dΩ = ⟨dP/dΩ⟩/⟨S⟩ = (e⁴/m_e²c⁴) sin²Θ = r_e² sin²Θ,  r_e ≡ e²/(m_ec²) classical electron radius
• Thomson scattering cross section σ_T = ∫(dσ_sca/dΩ)dΩ = (8π/3)r_e² = (8π/3)(e²/m_ec²)² = 0.665×10⁻²⁴ cm²
  – Independent of frequency

For Unpolarized Incident Light
• An unpolarized beam can be regarded as the independent superposition of two linear-polarized beams with perpendicular axes.
• Choose one such beam along E₁, which is in the plane of the incident (k̂) and scattered (n̂) directions, and the second along E₂, perpendicular to this plane.
• Then, (dσ/dΩ)_unpol = ½[(dσ(Θ)/dΩ)_pol + (dσ(π/2)/dΩ)_pol] = ½r_e²(1+sin²Θ) = ½r_e²(1+cos²θ)
  – Forward-backward symmetry: • Unchanged by θ → −θ
  – Total cross section: σ_unpol = ∫(dσ/dΩ)_unpol dΩ = (8π/3)r_e² = σ_T
[그림: E₁ 위쪽, k̂ 오른쪽, n̂은 k̂와 각 θ, E₁과 n̂ 사이 Θ = π/2 − θ, 앞쪽으로 E₂, E₂와 n̂ 사이 Θ = π/2]

Degree of Polarization
• Depend on the viewing angle with respect to the incident direction.  (dσ/dΩ)_unpol = ½r_e²(1+cos²θ)
[그림: 왼쪽 — 앞 슬라이드의 E₁·k̂·n̂·E₂ 좌표, n̂에 수직으로 'North' 빨간 화살표. 오른쪽 — Observer's plane of the sky: 위쪽(North) 화살표 길이 cos²θ, 오른쪽(E₂) 화살표 길이 1]
  I_min/I_max = cos²θ ➔ Π = (I_max − I_min)/(I_max + I_min) = (1 − cos²θ)/(1 + cos²θ)
  • No polarization along the incident direction (θ = 0)
  • 100% polarization in the perpendicular direction (θ = π/2)

Oscillator Model of an Atom
• Line radiation from atoms and ions is quantum mechanical processes, but one can use classical theory using damped oscillators to obtain approximate expression for radiated power.
• In the Lorentz oscillator model, an electron bound to a nucleus by a spring is in simple harmonic oscillations with frequency ω₀.
• EOM: ẍ = −ω₀²x  – Solution: x(t) = x₀cos(ω₀t)
• The total power radiated over one cycle is ⟨P⟩ = (2e²/3c³)⟨|ẍ|²⟩ = (2e²x₀²ω₀⁴/3c³)⟨cos²ω₀t⟩ = e²ω₀⁴x₀²/(3c³)

Radiation Damping
• Power from an oscillator means that it loses energy over time.
  – The kinetic energy of an electron is E₀ = m_eω₀²x₀²/2.
  – The radiated energy over one period is E_r = P/ω₀ = e²ω₀³x₀²/(3c³).
• If the radiation damping is weak (E_r ≪ E₀), or e²ω₀³x₀²/(3c³) ≪ ½m_eω₀²x₀²
  Or, if ω₀τ ≪ 1, one can treat the damping as small perturbations on the particle's motion.
  τ ≡ 2r_e/(3c) = 2e²/(3m_ec³) = 6.27×10⁻²⁴ s = the timescale for radiation to cross a distance r_e
  r_e ≡ e²/(m_ec²) = 2.82×10⁻¹³ cm = classical electron radius

Radiation Reaction Force
• There must be a force F_rad, called the radiation reaction force, acting on a particle by virtue of the radiation it produces.
• Since the energy radiated must be compensated for by the work done against F_rad, one is tempted to write −⟨F_rad·v⟩ = ⟨2e²v̇²/(3c³)⟩
• Since ⟨v̇²⟩ = (1/T)∫₀ᵀ v̇·v̇ dT = (1/T)∫₀ᵀ[d/dt(v·v̇) − v·v̈]dT = (1/T)[v·v̇]₀ᵀ − ⟨v·v̈⟩ = −⟨v·v̈⟩
  one can write F_rad = (2e²/3c³)v̈ = m_eτv̈ = −Γm_e v
  where the radiation damping constant is Γ = τω₀² = (2r_e/3c)ω₀² = (2e²/3m_ec³)ω₀² ≪ ω₀ for ω₀τ ≪ 1

Decaying Solution
• Thus, the EOM with the radiation reaction force is ẍ + Γẋ + ω₀²x = 0
• Take x ≡ x₀e^{αt} as a solution to obtain α² + Γα + ω₀² = 0, which for Γ ≪ ω₀ gives α ≈ ±iω₀ − Γ/2
• For the initial conditions of x(0) = x₀ and ẋ(0) = 0, the solution becomes x(t) = x₀cos ω₀t · e^{−Γt/2}
• That is, the energy of an electron decays as ∝ exp(−Γt), with timescale of τ_life ≡ 1/Γ = 3m_ec³/(2e²ω₀²) = 1/(ω₀²τ) (≫ 1/ω₀)

FT of x(t)
• The EM radiation emitted does not have one frequency ν₀ = ω₀/(2π), but has a frequency distribution.
• Let us write the solution x(t) as x(t) = x₀cos(ω₀t)e^{−Γt/2} = (x₀/2)(e^{iω₀t} + e^{−iω₀t})e^{−Γt/2}
• Fourier transform of x(t) assuming that x(t) = 0 for t < 0:
  x̃(ω) = (1/2π)∫_{−∞}^{+∞} x(t)e^{iωt}dt = (x₀/4π)∫₀^∞ dt[e^{(iω+iω₀−Γ/2)t} + e^{(iω−iω₀−Γ/2)t}]
  = (x₀/4π)[1/(Γ/2 − i(ω+ω₀)) + 1/(Γ/2 − i(ω−ω₀))] ≈ (x₀/4π)·1/(Γ/2 − i(ω−ω₀))  for ω > 0
  ➡ |x̃|² = (x₀/4π)² · 1/[(ω−ω₀)² + (Γ/2)²]

FT of E(t)
• To obtain the emitted spectrum, we need to take FT of E_rad(x,t) = (q/c)[n̂×{n̂×β̇}/R]_ret ➡ E(t) = −e n̂×[n̂×ẍ(t)]/(c²r)
• Since x(t) = ∫x̃(ω)e^{−iωt}dω ➡ ẍ(t) = −ω²∫x̃(ω)e^{−iωt}dω, we obtain Ẽ(ω) = (eω²/c²r) n̂×[n̂×x̃(ω)]
• Therefore, Ẽ(ω) = (eω²/c²r) x̃(ω) sinΘ, where Θ is an angle between p̈ and an observer.
[그림: 전하 q에서 위로 p̈ 화살표, p̈와 각 Θ를 이루는 n̂ 방향 끝에 E_rad와 B_rad(지면 안팎)]

Energy Spectrum
• Since the radiation energy per unit area per unit angular frequency is given by dW/(dA dω) = c|Ẽ(ω)|², we obtain the energy spectrum
  dW/dω = ∫c|Ẽ(ω)|² r² dΩ = (e²ω⁴/c³)|x̃|²∫sin²Θ dΩ ≃ (8πe²ω⁴/3c³)(x₀/4π)² · 1/[(ω−ω₀)² + (Γ/2)²]
  (옆에 다시 적힌 식: Ẽ(ω) = (eω²/c²r)x̃(ω)sinΘ,  |x̃|² = (x₀/4π)²/[(ω−ω₀)² + (Γ/2)²])

Classical Line Width
• Or by taking ω ~ ω₀ in the numerator, dW/dω = (m_eΓω₀²x₀²/4π) · 1/[(ω−ω₀)² + (Γ/2)²] = ½m_eω₀²x₀²φ(ω)
  where φ(ω) ≡ (1/π)(Γ/2)/[(ω−ω₀)² + (Γ/2)²] with ∫_{−∞}^{+∞}φ(ω)dω = 1 is a Lorenzian line shape function.
• Total energy radiated from an oscillator is W = ∫_{−∞}^{+∞}(dW/dω)dω = ½m_eω₀²x₀² = the initial energy of the oscillator.
• FWHM: Δω_FWHM = Γ.
• Since λ = c/ν = 2πc/ω, Δλ_FWHM = 2πcΔω_FWHM/ω₀² = 2πc/(ω₀²τ_life) = 2πcτ = 1.18×10⁻⁴ Å  Natural line width

Atoms in a Radiation Field
• Modeled by a driven damped oscillator
• EOM: ẍ + Γẋ + ω₀²x = (eE₀/m_e)e^{iωt}
• Solution: x(t) = [(e/m_e)E₀/(ω₀² − ω² + iΓω)]e^{iωt} = [(e/m_e)E₀/√((ω₀²−ω²)² + (Γω)²)]e^{i(ωt+δ)}, where δ = −tan⁻¹(Γω/(ω₀²−ω²))
• Time-averaged total power is ⟨P⟩ = (2e²/3c³)⟨|v̇|²⟩ = (2e²/3c³)(e/m_e)²E₀²ω⁴/[(ω²−ω₀²)² + Γ²ω²]⟨cos²(ωt+δ)⟩ = (e⁴E₀²/3m_e²c³)·ω⁴/[(ω²−ω₀²)² + Γ²ω²]

Scattering Cross Section
• Since ⟨S⟩ = (c/8π)E₀², the scattering cross section by an oscillator is σ = ⟨P⟩/⟨S⟩ = (8πe⁴/3m_e²c⁴)·ω⁴/[(ω²−ω₀²)² + Γ²ω²] = σ_T ω⁴/[(ω²−ω₀²)² + Γ²ω²]
[그림: σ/σ_T(세로, 0–30) vs ω/ω₀(가로, 0–4) — ω/ω₀=1에서 뾰족한 피크(폭 Γ/ω₀ 표시), 저주파 쪽 '∝ω⁴', 고주파에서 1로 수렴]
• For ω ≫ ω₀, σ → σ_T: Thomson scattering – At high energy, the binding becomes negligible.
• For ω ≪ ω₀, σ = σ_T(ω/ω₀)⁴: Rayleigh scattering – Responsible for the blue color of the sky and the red color of the sun at sunrise and sunset.
• For ω ≈ ω₀: resonant scattering – Corresponding to the case in QM where an electron becomes excited by absorbing radiation and then de-excited back to the original level.

Resonant Scattering
• At ω ≈ ω₀, one can simplify the denominator by using (ω²−ω₀²)² = (ω−ω₀)²(ω+ω₀)² ≈ 4ω₀²(ω−ω₀)² to obtain σ ≈ (σ_T/4)·ω₀²/[(ω−ω₀)² + (Γ/2)²] = (πe²/m_ec)φ(ν), with φ(ν) = (1/π)[(Γ/4π)/((ν−ν₀)² + (Γ/4π)²)]
• Total (classical) cross section: ∫₀^∞ σ dν = πe²/(m_ec) = 0.0265 cm² s⁻¹
• In QM, ∫₀^∞ σ(ν)dν = (πe²/m_ec) f₁₂, where f₁₂ is the oscillator strength (or f-value), representing the QM correction for the classical result for line transitions.
